tweets: Brahma is credited with creating the entire universe. Yet across India you will find millions of temples to Shiva and Vishnu, and almost none to him. One of the only surviving ones stands in a small Rajasthan town: Pushkar.

Legend holds Brahma chose this spot for a great yajna, and let a lotus (pushpa) fall from his hand to mark the ground. The flower became a lake, and the town took its name: Pushkar, from pushpa plus kar, hand.

Why so few Brahma temples anywhere? Puranic legend says his wife Savitri, left out of that yajna, cursed him to go unworshipped elsewhere. Pushkar stayed the exception, and both the Mahabharata and Padma Purana mark it as a sacred tirtha sages journeyed to.

The lake is still ringed by 52 ghats, revered as one of Hinduism's most sacred bathing sites. Pilgrims gather here every Kartik Purnima, when Pushkar also fills with its famous camel fair, sacred geography thousands of years old by tradition, still very much alive. 🪷
